turns.content: I've noticed my drinking has crept up, most nights now, more than I'd admit to anyone, and I'm trying to decide whether to actually do something about it or keep telling myself it's fine because I still function.
You know it's not fine. You want to stop drinking so much. You already see the problem. What you do now is clear: stop drinking or get help. That is true.
Nobody's confronted me, which I keep taking as proof it's not a problem, even though I'm the one lying awake thinking about it.
You're aware of the problem. You want to address it. You do something about it now.
The idea of telling my partner feels like handing over something I can't take back.
You want honesty with your partner. You do tell them the truth. That is what you want.
I poured out the bottle last night, felt proud, and bought another one today. That pattern is the thing I can't keep pretending I don't see.
You see the pattern. You want to break it. You stop buying the bottles.
